headline: High: Chatwoot’s customer-data workflows plus Authelia’s broad network egress create leakage and compliance risk if they are connected through shared auth or support integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, while Chatwoot exposes integrations and support content flows. No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt-injection is not proven; the only plausible bridge is unusual manual or integration-based content transfer, which keeps blast radius limited.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is manually copied into an Authelia-managed auth or policy workflow
IF an integration forwards Chatwoot messages into a shared file or queue that Authelia parses
mitigations: Disable any ad hoc copy-paste bridge between support text and auth policy inputs.
Restrict integrations to structured fields only.
Add a short provenance note to any imported content.
Review ForwardAuth mappings before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages; Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces. If they share a workspace or auth context, sensitive support data could flow into outbound requests or logs. The pairwise path is inferred, but the data classes make the blast radius material.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are passed into Authelia-backed auth or proxy logs
IF both agents are deployed under a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal
mitigations: Separate support data from auth logs.
Turn off verbose request logging.
Use distinct service accounts.
Mask customer identifiers before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is non-runnable here and has no filesystem-write capability listed; Chatwoot is also not shown with filesystem or git write permissions. With only broad network egress on both sides, overlapping mutable-resource conflict is not established, so the conflict surface appears small.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking
mitigations: Keep separate deployment directories.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Document ownership of any shared resource.
Add lock files if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot’s support workflows can consume external content, and Authelia’s auth outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream systems. If Chatwoot renders or acts on Authelia-derived claims without verification, a mistaken auth decision can cascade into incorrect support actions or access handling. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Chatwoot uses Authelia output as a trusted source for customer identity or entitlement
IF downstream support actions are triggered without a verification step
mitigations: Require a human verification step for identity claims.
Display auth assertions as untrusted metadata.
Log the source of each assertion.
Limit automated actions from auth-derived fields.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for imported claims.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot explicitly touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Authelia has broad network egress and auth/proxy surfaces. If customer or identity data flows from Chatwoot into Authelia-hosted logs or third-party endpoints, a compliance breach can occur by default unless the operator intervenes. The evidence is docs-only, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is processed by Authelia in a jurisdiction or retention regime that differs from the source system
IF auth or proxy logs retain customer identifiers beyond the support system’s policy
mitigations: Review data-flow maps before deployment.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Set retention to the shortest compliant window.
Separate regional deployments by data residency.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based log redaction.
